title: Adaptive Accent System and Rollout Legend for Compact Dashboard Cards
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Compact dashboard cards across the Console need a lightweight visual system to communicate rollout state, traffic split, and cost sensitivity without expanding vertical space. Current visual signals (pills + large banners) are too verbose for dense grids and cause inconsistent usage across teams.

Goal: Define an adaptive accent/token system and a compact rollout legend component that: 1) fits into 36–56px card headers, 2) scales across compact/regular/dense density tokens, 3) maintains WCAG AA contrast for text and icons, 4) maps consistently to the Console's rollout states (Canary, Gradual, Stable, Fallback), and 5) is available as a Figma component and code-ready variant matrix.

Deliverables:
- Figma component kit with 3 density variants, color accent tokens, and iconography set.
- A standalone "Rollout Legend" component (tooltip-enabled) that expands from a micro-indicator in the card header.
- Token mapping doc: token names, fallback values, and runtime props for front-end implementation (density, accent,-muted/hover states).
- Accessibility guidelines and contrast test snapshots.
- Prototype demonstrating 120-card grid rendering, keyboard focus states, and tooltip interactions for small-screen widths.
acceptance_criteria: Figma master components for Card Accent and Rollout Legend with three density variants (dense, default, comfortable)
Color and semantic tokens defined (accent.primary, accent.warning, accent.neutral-muted) with hex + accessible contrast examples
Rollout Legend has keyboard-accessible expansion and reads state via ARIA attributes
Engineering sign-off on variant props and a sample implementation PR linked
Performance: prototype renders 120 cards in a grid within Chrome with no dropped frames during hover/tooltip interactions
design_notes:
2026-03-10: Kickoff — scoped problem with PM and Eng. Agreed to prioritize density-first approach and token-first handoff.
2026-03-11: Initial Figma pass created: micro-accent swatch (6px stripe), compact state icon (8px), tooltip pattern to surface rollout metadata on hover/focus.
2026-03-12: Trade-offs discussed with Eng (Mateo): prefer CSS custom properties for runtime density mapping to avoid large variant proliferation in code. Decided to expose three runtime props: --card-density, --accent-intent, --legend-mode.
2026-03-13: Accessibility pass with Priya — adjusted accent palette to increase contrast for 'canary' yellow -> warm-amber and added an outline-focus style for 2px to meet keyboard visibility.
Notes on trade-offs: Keeping visual subtlety vs. explicitness — opted for micro-accent + optional legend expansion to avoid visual clutter in dense dashboards. For high-priority incidents, the system allows an override to show a larger banner (out of scope for this ticket).
review_feedback: PM (Aisha): likes density-first approach; requested telemetry hooks so usage of legend toggles can be measured
Engineering (Mateo): requested explicit token names and fallback order for CSS vars, plus a small sample React component in the PR
Design Systems (Priya): asked for contrast examples at 90%, 75%, and 50% opacity to ensure token behavior when layered over images or gradients
Accessibility (external audit): suggested adding aria-live region for rollout state changes when automated rollouts progress
next_steps: Finalize Figma tokens and publish to the shared design system library (owner: Priya)
Add token mapping doc in the Console repo and open engineering PR for sample component (assignee: Mateo)
Instrument telemetry for legend toggles and card-density switch (owner: Oliver)
Run cross-team review in design sync (date: 2026-03-18) and capture sign-offs
comments: 2026-03-11 Maya: Uploaded first Figma frames for review. 2026-03-12 Mateo: Commented on CSS var naming and requested fallback strategy. 2026-03-13 Priya: Accessibility pass complete; suggested small color tweak to amber. 2026-03-13 Aisha: Approved prioritization and asked to measure impact on time-to-understand for new users.
customer_notes: This work reduces cognitive load for customers monitoring many rollouts simultaneously and aims to make rollout state scannable at a glance in dense operational views.
